notes: I'm keeping the 206 separate groups, and this is the same answer as before. This isn't a real error I can fix from the material provided.

The attached booklet has only two pages: the back cover and a page showing other Friends sets (3184, 3189, 3061, 3315). It has no building steps, so nothing in it says which piece sits on which. Any connection I added would be invented.

Set 3316-1 is an advent calendar whose 24 daily gifts are separate small builds (and loose accessories). So it really does come as many unconnected groups. The expected count is around 24, not 206, because the real builds would join pieces within each day.

graph_initial.title: LEGO Friends Advent Calendar 2012 (3316-1)
notes: The attached booklet contains only two pages: the back cover (warnings, a plane image, LEGO Friends artwork) and a page showing other Friends sets (3184, 3189, 3061, 3315). No building steps, sub-assemblies or callouts were included.
Because no step pages were visible, I could not read which pieces go together, their order, positions or connections. I did not invent them from memory of the 24 daily mini-builds.
All 206 pieces from the PIECE LIST appear exactly once. Each has step=1 (placeholder), rests_on=[] and position=null (unplaced loose parts). No other_joins are recorded.
To fill in real steps, positions, rests_on and pin/clip joins, the full instruction booklet pages are needed.

final_issue_list: the build is 206 separate groups of pieces; connect them unless the booklet really builds separate models
